wordpress-com-mcp-api.$comment: Identifies requests to the WordPress.com hosted MCP server (public-api.wordpress.com).

wordpress-com-mcp-session.$comment: Open and maintain an MCP session: initialize, list tools/prompts/resources, ping, and send notifications. Required for any MCP client to function; does not read or modify WordPress.com content.

wordpress-com-mcp-read-all.$comment: Run any read-only WordPress.com MCP operation (view posts, pages, comments, media, site design, site settings and stats, plugins, users, your account, domains and plans; list and describe the available operations) plus the MCP session handshake. Nothing is created, changed, deleted or purchased.

wordpress-com-mcp-write-all.$comment: Run any WordPress.com MCP operation that creates, changes or deletes something (content, site design, site settings, plugins, users, your account and subscriptions, DNS records, new sites) or sends feedback to WordPress.com, plus the MCP session handshake.

wordpress-com-mcp-read-content.$comment: View posts, pages, custom content, comments, media, categories, tags and patterns on your sites, and search their content.

wordpress-com-mcp-write-content.$comment: Create and edit posts, pages, custom content, comments, media, categories, tags and patterns on your sites, including rearranging the sections of a post or page. Does not delete anything.

wordpress-com-mcp-delete-content.$comment: Delete posts, pages, custom content, comments, media, categories, tags and patterns from your sites.

wordpress-com-mcp-read-design.$comment: View how your sites look: the active theme and its styles and presets, templates, template parts, navigation menus, widgets, global styles and available themes.

wordpress-com-mcp-write-design.$comment: Change how your sites look: create, edit or delete templates, template parts, navigation menus, menu items and widgets, and update global styles.

wordpress-com-mcp-read-sites.$comment: List your sites and view their settings, statistics, activity log, installed plugins, themes, users, backup, security scan, uptime monitor, newsletter and launch status. Also check whether a site address is available, and search public sites that have opted in to AI agents.

wordpress-com-mcp-write-sites.$comment: Change site-wide settings: update settings, switch the theme, launch a site or change its visibility, run a security scan, turn the uptime monitor and account protection on or off, change newsletter settings and add subscribers, and create new WordPress.com sites.

wordpress-com-mcp-read-plugins.$comment: See which plugins are installed on your sites and search the plugin directory.

wordpress-com-mcp-write-plugins.$comment: Install, upload, activate, deactivate, update or uninstall plugins on your sites.

wordpress-com-mcp-read-users.$comment: See the people who have access to your sites, their roles and pending invitations.

wordpress-com-mcp-write-users.$comment: Invite people to your sites, resend or cancel invitations, change roles and remove access.

wordpress-com-mcp-read-account.$comment: View your WordPress.com account: profile, notification settings and inbox, achievements, connected services, security status, subscriptions, invoices and renewals. Also view WordPress.com plans and prices and prepare checkout links (payment always happens in your browser, never through the agent).

wordpress-com-mcp-write-account.$comment: Change your WordPress.com account: update your profile and notification settings, stop or resume subscription renewals, remove a payment method, move a subscription to another site, and change your billing currency.

wordpress-com-mcp-read-domains.$comment: View your domains and their DNS records, and search for available domains with their prices and checkout links (payment always happens in your browser, never through the agent).

wordpress-com-mcp-write-domains.$comment: Change your domains: add or remove DNS records, restore default DNS records, change nameservers, set up an external mail service, attach a domain to a site and set the primary domain. These changes affect live traffic and email delivery.

wordpress-com-mcp-send-feedback.$comment: Send a feature request, bug report or other feedback about the MCP server to the WordPress.com team.
